question: What primary factor distinguishes a professional nurse-patient relationship from a social relationship?

options.A: It relies entirely on mutual sharing of personal lives
options.B: It is sustained purely by financial compensation
options.C: It only occurs outside the hospital setting
options.D: It is strictly client-centered and goal-oriented

explanation: Professional nursing relationships exist solely to meet the health needs of the patient rather than mutual social fulfillment. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why must a nurse avoid seeking personal emotional fulfillment from a patient?

options.A: Hospital policies prohibit any friendly conversation at the bedside
options.B: Patients are legally forbidden from offering emotional comfort
options.C: It shifts the focus away from the client-centered goals of care
options.D: It automatically guarantees a breach of medical confidentiality

explanation: When a nurse looks to a patient to meet their own social or emotional needs, the dynamic blurs into a social relationship and compromises professional objectivity. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which nursing theorist is best known for defining nursing as an interpersonal therapeutic process?
explanation: Peplau's interpersonal theory emphasizes the nurse-patient relationship as the core foundation of nursing practice. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary clinical value of establishing trust early in the nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: It encourages the patient to share accurate health history and concerns
options.B: It prevents the patient from ever questioning treatment plans
options.C: It guarantees the patient will pay hospital bills on time
options.D: It eliminates the need for any further diagnostic tests

explanation: Patients who trust their nurse feel psychologically safe enough to disclose sensitive symptoms and fears necessary for proper diagnosis and care. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h2)

question: During which phase of the nurse-patient relationship does the nurse examine their own personal biases before meeting the client?
explanation: The pre-interaction phase happens before direct contact, allowing the nurse to prepare and check personal prejudices. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h3)

question: A patient is being discharged from the surgical ward today. What primary task should the nurse focus on during this final stage of the relationship?

options.A: Reviewing progress made and facilitating a smooth transition of care
options.B: Initiating a brand new diagnostic workup for chronic joint pain
options.C: Withholding discharge instructions to prolong the hospital stay
options.D: Exchanging personal phone numbers for future social hangouts

explanation: The termination phase centers on summarizing gains, ensuring continuity of care, and achieving a healthy closure. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which communication technique gives a patient the freedom to direct their response and share their story fully?

options.D: Using closed-ended yes or no queries

explanation: Open-ended questions prevent restricted answers and encourage patients to elaborate on their thoughts and feelings. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is the observation of non-verbal cues critical during patient interactions?

options.A: Patients are legally mandated to hide their symptoms verbally
options.B: Non-verbal signals often reveal true emotions that words attempt to hide
options.C: Medical staff rely exclusively on written lab results instead
options.D: Spoken words always completely contradict physical health status

explanation: Body language, posture, and facial expressions frequently betray underlying distress or fear when a patient verbally claims everything is fine. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized barrier to therapeutic interpersonal relationships?
explanation: Active listening is a fundamental tool for building relationships, whereas stereotyping, cultural divides, and environmental noise act as barriers. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h5)

question: How does heavy staff workload negatively impact nurse-patient relationships?

options.A: It causes rushing, leaving patients feeling neglected and unimportant
options.B: It automatically eliminates cultural and language barriers
options.C: It gives nurses extra time to sit and talk with patients
options.D: It improves the accuracy of non-verbal communication

explanation: When nurses are severely overworked, interactions become rushed and transactional, destroying the opportunity to build genuine rapport. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h5)

question: What term describes the space where a nurse's behavior is safe, effective, and focused entirely on the patient's wellbeing?
explanation: The zone of helpfulness represents the ideal professional distance between under-involvement and destructive over-involvement. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is a primary risk associated with a nurse crossing professional boundaries into over-involvement?

options.A: The nurse loses objectivity and can no longer provide safe clinical judgment
options.B: The patient immediately recovers and requires no further hospital care
options.C: The patient will lose all forms of health insurance coverage
options.D: Hospital administration will automatically promote the nurse

explanation: Over-involvement compromises professional objectivity, often leading to biased care, burnout, and ethical violations. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h6)

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication framework stand for?
explanation: SBAR is a standardized interprofessional communication tool used to structure critical patient reports concisely. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is poor communication among members of the healthcare team dangerous for patients?

options.A: It results in lower hospital utility bills
options.B: It can lead to medical errors, missed interventions, and compromised safety
options.C: It forces doctors to spend less time writing paperwork
options.D: It automatically shortens the duration of patient visits

explanation: When team members fail to share vital clinical updates clearly, critical details fall through the cracks, directly threatening patient safety. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of self-reflection in developing nursing relational skills?

options.A: To assess the physical cleanliness of patient wards
options.B: To memorize hospital administrative bylaws word-for-word
options.C: To calculate daily medication dosages more rapidly
options.D: To evaluate one's communication patterns and emotional triggers

explanation: Self-reflection allows nurses to identify personal biases and emotional responses that might interfere with objective patient care. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h8)

question: A newly qualified nurse frequently feels frustrated when a patient repeatedly asks the same questions about surgery. What strategy will best help this nurse improve their relational response?

options.A: Reporting the patient to the hospital disciplinary committee
options.B: Relying solely on written pamphlets without speaking to the patient
options.C: Avoiding the patient's room for the rest of the shift
options.D: Practicing self-reflection and empathy to understand the root of the patient's fear

explanation: Repetitive questioning usually stems from high anxiety; empathy and reflection help the nurse respond with patience and reassurance. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h8)
